title: SalusTransform: Evaluation of Interventions for Equitable Health-Promoting Urban Development and the Great Transformation
summary:
Cities and neighborhoods should be places where people can live healthy lives, where social inequalities are reduced, and where sustainability plays a central role. But how well do current urban development strategies achieve these goals? This is the question at the heart of the SalusTransform project.
Many municipalities in Germany implement what are known as Integrated Urban Development Concepts (ISEK) to improve housing quality, mobility, green spaces, and social infrastructure. These concepts include a wide range of different measures, but so far, research has mainly focused on their planning and implementation—little is known about whether and how they actually change people's living conditions. SalusTransform aims to close this gap by comparing neighborhoods in Bremen, Bochum, and Wuppertal: in each city, one district with an existing urban development concept is analyzed alongside a district without such a concept.
Together with city administrations, local stakeholders, and residents, the project examines which measures have been implemented and to what extent they contribute to creating healthier, more socially equitable, and environmentally sustainable urban areas. The insights gained will help shape future urban development strategies, ensuring they are even more closely aligned with the needs of residents while promoting long-term sustainable structures.
